title: feat: unify locator and expectation matching
description:
<!-- Kata: zm3j -->

## Summary

- Replace locator `has_text` and `predicate` with one `match` argument: an exact string, a reusable `pz_regex()` pattern, or a JavaScript function described by `pz_js()`.
- Use the same JavaScript regex and whitespace rules for locators and text, value, attribute, URL, and title expectations. Bare strings compare exactly; remove the old expectation `match`/`.match` modes and competing R-regex path.
- Add named `ignore_case` and `fixed` options, with Unicode-aware regex matching. Preserve lazy resolution, matching before `which`, auto-wait, scope behavior, pairwise character vectors, and missing-value rules.
- Migrate examples and documentation, including the bundled skill and rendered README. Cover callback return requirements, restrictive CSP, Unicode, invalid patterns, empty/missing values, negation, and cross-module seams.

## Verification

```r
library(paparazzi)

pz_with_page(pz_example("tasks"), function(page) {
  passport <- pz_loc(".task-title", match = pz_regex("^Renew"))
  pz_expect_text(page, "Renew passport", target = passport)
  pz_expect_text(page, pz_regex("passport"), target = passport)

  high <- pz_loc(
    ".task",
    match = pz_js('el => el.dataset.priority === "high"')
  )
  pz_expect_attr(page, high, `data-priority` = "high")
})
```

- Full local suite: no failures or warnings; final documentation/matcher checks also pass.
- `air format --check .`, `jarl check .`, and diff checks pass.
- Completed-unit roborev review 1632 and human documentation review addressed; generated help examples verified.

This is an intentional breaking API change in an unreleased package. No compatibility aliases are retained.

title: Rename `pz_js()` to `pz_evaluate()`
description:
## Summary

Renames the exported `pz_js()` to `pz_evaluate()` across sources, tests, and docs. paparazzi is unreleased, so this is a hard rename with no deprecation alias.

Why the new name:

- **`evaluate` is the term of art** for "run JS in the page and return the result" across Playwright (`page.evaluate()`), Puppeteer, and the Chrome DevTools Protocol (`Runtime.evaluate`). paparazzi pitches itself as Playwright lite, so the reference API's vocabulary is the one users — and coding agents — will guess first. (Observed in the wild: an agent using paparazzi hallucinated `pz_eval()` when it needed this function.)
- **`pz_js()` was a noun, not a verb.** In the R ecosystem, bare `JS()` functions (shiny, htmlwidgets) *tag* a string as JavaScript for use elsewhere, so `pz_js()` read like a marker/constructor rather than an action.
- **Discovery runs on the prefix.** Users find functions by typing `pz_ev...` into autocomplete, so the discriminating token belongs at the front of the name; verb-first naming does that work.

Housekeeping:

- `R/js.R` and `tests/testthat/test-js.R` keep their names — the file houses the JS family (`pz_evaluate()`, `pz_chromote()`, `js_value()`), not just the renamed function.
- `man/` and `NAMESPACE` regenerated; `_pkgdown.yml` reference updated; NEWS bullet added; `.agents/SPEC.md` updated (caught in review — hidden directory the original sweep skipped).

title: DNM: diagnostics for Windows framed-capture hang (kata 273h)
description:
Draft experiment for kata 273h — do not merge.

The merged staging refactor added a second framed capture (on the staging source page) to test-frame.R's leak test; on windows-latest (release) that call hangs 10s waiting on Page.captureScreenshot, 2/2 runs. This branch adds three diagnostic variants in tests/testthat/test-zz-273h.R to separate hypotheses in one Windows cycle:

- **273h-A**: staging source captured first — does the hang follow the page or the second-capture position?
- **273h-B**: two framed captures with no staging — is pz_stage_frame required?
- **273h-C**: original order with a 30s timeout — slow vs truly wedged?

The original leak test still runs and is expected to fail; that is the control. Only windows-latest (release) matters here.

title: test: skip browser and system-tool tests on CRAN, guard CRAN-simulated runs
description:
## Summary

Closes the CRAN detritus problem (kata d6w5) by making CRAN safety a property of the test suite rather than of cleanup:

- **Skips**: `skip_on_cran()` now guards every test path that launches Chrome, the Quarto CLI, a Shiny app subprocess, or av/gifski encoding. The suite previously had zero CRAN skips, so CRAN machines with Chrome installed (e.g. the macOS builder) would run the entire browser suite.
- **Guard**: new `setup-cran-guard.R` — when `NOT_CRAN != "true"`, points `CHROMOTE_CHROME`/`QUARTO_PATH` at nonexistent paths so any missed skip errors loudly, and a teardown sweep fails the run if a browser object or Chrome/Quarto/Crashpad detritus exists. It immediately caught two real skip bypasses (fixed here).
- **Cleanup**: new `setup-00-subprocess-tmpdir.R` scopes `TMPDIR`/`TEMP`/`TMP` to a session-owned directory removed at teardown, eliminating the `com.google.Chrome.*` / `chrome_chrome_url_fetcher_.*` / `quarto-session*` detritus NOTE on the full matrix without hiding the check or deleting from shared temp dirs.
- **CI**: two new `as-cran` matrix variants (ubuntu, macOS) run the check with `NOT_CRAN=false`. Chrome and Quarto stay installed on these jobs so the guard has teeth; macOS mirrors the CRAN builder that ships Chrome.

## Validation

- Full local gate with `NOT_CRAN=true CI=true`: 0 failures, 0 warnings
- Simulated-CRAN run (`NOT_CRAN=false`): 0 failures, 901 tests skip "On CRAN"
- Sabotage check (removing a skip) fails the run hard, as designed
- air format, jarl, git diff --check all clean
